item.description: The first hurricane of the Atlantic season was forecast to intensify rapidly and cause dangerous conditions in the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi when it makes landfall late Friday or early Saturday.

item.title: Super El Niño is here. What's so super about it?
item.description: This year, federal forecasters say the planet could see the strongest El Niño event on record. Here's what you need to know.

item.title: Studying this super El Niño could save lives. NOAA is scaling back research
item.description: A powerful El Niño is already influencing extreme weather around the planet. During the last strong El Niño, federal agencies ramped up research in the hope of improving weather forecasts. This year, they won't be matching that effort.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
item.description: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.
